kill_argument: check-methods validates the estimators (Prop 99, TWFE identities) and the inference only through its own Monte Carlo reimplementation (mc_dd, mc_T); nothing in it runs the path the study runs use to turn placebos into labels: estimate -> placebo_inference -> crit_for/nu_for_donors (L quantile, t at nu, SDID floor) -> intervals -> h2_label -> verdict. So the first end-to-end execution of that path would be on real post-2023Q3 data, and a wiring error (wrong statistic's critical values, wrong pool floor, a mislabelled CI) would surface only as a result. I attacked this and it held: on synthetic panels only (no study data), I ran select_rule, level_mde and every post-period, verdict and figure script for a DDT-POPW-P-D20 and an SDID-E-D20 primary; all 24 candidates recover a noise-free -0.03 effect exactly; the run path equals mc_dd/mc_T to 0 for DD and DDT (tau, SE_s, SE_n, every placebo); label_probabilities matches 400,000 simulated draws within Monte Carlo error; the full-panel and pre-panel seasonal adjustments agree exactly on 2014-2019; the SDID floor, nu over own donors (rob-7225 J = 18) and the other-pool statistic reach the runs as the design says. What remains is undisclosed choices and caption wording, not wrong numbers.

findings.text: The year-1 and year-2 one-sided H1 wage tests use the pooled H1 statistic's critical values and nu: h1_wage.py calls crit_for(m_lvl, 'h1', ...) once and applies the same c and nu to 'pooled', 'y1' and 'y2'. level-mde computes no yearly W statistic. Neither the design nor runs/NOTES.md item 5 states this choice (item 5 covers anticip and h3-years' yearly employment ATTs, not the yearly wage tests). The choice is not inert: h1_y1_reject and h1_y2_reject gate the yearly own-wage elasticities in h3_years.py (owe_y1, owe_y2 are 'not computed' unless they reject), which the claims plan lists.
findings.evidence: code/h1_wage.py lines 29-39; code/h3_years.py lines 63-71; code/level_mde.py families() (h1 family has only 'pooled'); runs/NOTES.md item 5; plan.json design.method IMPLEMENTATION CHOICES 5 and DECISIONS; design.analysis_plan[7] ('the one-sided 5% test for each'). Remedy (cheapest): add the choice to NOTES item 5 and to the design's implementation choices before h1-wage runs; alternative: add yearly W statistics to level-mde.
findings.response: PI: recorded as design deviation D5 before any analysis run; the paper states it.

findings.text: If select picks an SDID candidate, the figure captions misdescribe the intervals: fig_event.py and fig_placebo.py print the critical values as 't at nu with the decision-set quantile as a floor', but for an SDID statistic crit_for also applies the Monte Carlo floor q_cal (design.method C1), which can bind (in runs/check-methods every q_cal value except R50 lo05 lies beyond the t_J value). The captions are generated text the Writer is told to use as is. Separately, the import prologue and comments in figlib.py, fig_event.py, fig_select.py and fig_placebo.py still say code/select.py shadows the standard 'select' module; select.py no longer exists (C4), so the comments are stale (harmless to the numbers).
findings.evidence: code/fig_event.py caption lines 202-206; code/fig_placebo.py caption lines 144-146; code/sclib.py crit_for and critical_values (floor argument); code/level_mde.py sdid_floor_<key>; code/figlib.py docstring lines 12-15; code/fig_*.py lines 22-29. Remedy: make each caption say whether the SDID floor applies (e.g. from runs/level-mde sdid_floor_h2, declared as an input, or a flag written by event-path and h2-emp), and drop or reword the stale prologue comments.
